newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent drifts sideways, gas oil weaker with hea.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent drifts sideways, gas oil weaker with hea.

text.p: IPE Brent futures drifted sideways after the NYMEX open on Tuesday, while gas oil slid from earlier highs as U.S. heating oil quickly retraced early gains, brokers said.
"Heating oil made its opening call but it's coming right off now," said one dealer.
March Brent was trading 16 cents up at $22.70 a barrel at 1518 GMT, off a session high of $22.74. Feb gas oil was up $2.50 a tonne at $206.50, having touched a high of $208.25 earlier.
Dealers said that jitters in the Brent futures market were keeping it rangebound.
Brent is in a very tight range, it's consolidating," a dealer said.
"Some people went a bit long in the runup last week and had the stuffing knocked out of them at the end," he added.

NYMEX heating oil made gains on overnight ACCESS trading on expectations of bullish distillate stock data to be released after the close of trade today. But heating oil quickly dipped off early highs shortly after the open.
Preliminary forecasts predicted that American Petroleum Institute (API) oil inventory data for the week ended Jan 31 would show a two million barrel draw in distillate stocks.
But comparisons with year-ago data could be bearish, analysts said.

"Distillate stocks relative to year-ago are worth watching - if the current deficit turns into a surplus there could be a negative psychological impact on the market," GNI's Leslie Nicholas said in a daily report.
Meanwhile, the weather looked set to undermine the heating oil market and the oil complex in general.
Temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, are expected to trend above normal this week, said independent forecaster Weather Services Corp.
